According to the Bhattiprolu inscription, who was the ruler in the 3rd century BC?
x:
The Bhattiprolu inscriptions, among the earliest inscriptions discovered in Andhra Pradesh, mention Kubhiraka as the local ruler. These inscriptions are associated with the famous Bhattiprolu Stupa and are important for understanding the political and religious history of Andhra during the 3rd century BCE. They also preserve one of the earliest forms of the Bhattiprolu script, considered an early regional variation of the Brahmi script.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Which inscription mentions the Nigama Sabha of the Satavahanas?
x:
The Nanaghat Inscription of Queen Naganika, wife of Satakarni I, refers to the Nigama Sabha (Assembly of Merchants). The inscription is one of the earliest and most important sources for understanding the administration, trade, merchant guilds and political history of the Satavahanas. It also records royal genealogies and Vedic sacrifices performed by the rulers.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: What was the royal language of the Satavahanas?
x:
The official and royal language of the Satavahanas was Prakrit. Most Satavahana inscriptions and coins are written in Prakrit using the Brahmi script. Literary works such as Gatha Saptasati, composed by King Hala, were also written in Maharashtri Prakrit.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: All the inscriptions of the Satavahanas were written in:
x:
The Satavahana rulers generally issued their inscriptions in Prakrit language using the Brahmi script. Famous examples include: • Nashik Inscription • Nanaghat Inscription • Karle Inscription • Kanheri Inscription Prakrit served as the official administrative language of the Satavahanas, while Brahmi was the script used for engraving inscriptions across the Deccan.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
